codes.title: Session expired
codes.meaning: You were signed out, usually after 12 hours or after signing in somewhere else.
codes.fix: Sign in again. Your work that was already saved is safe.

codes.title: Not allowed
codes.meaning: Your account does not have the role this action needs (for example, only the Editor-in-Chief can record decisions, only admins can publish).
codes.fix: Check you are signed in with the right account. If you should have access, ask the journal office to check your appointment or admin flag.

codes.title: Wrong email or password
codes.meaning: The email and password do not match an account.
codes.fix: Check for typing errors, or use Forgot password. Admins can reset a password from Apps Script with setPassword().

codes.title: Email not verified
codes.meaning: The account exists but its email address has not been confirmed.
codes.fix: Click the verification link in your email. A new one is sent each time you try to sign in.

codes.title: Link not valid
codes.meaning: The link is wrong, was already used, or was replaced by a newer email.
codes.fix: Use the most recent email. If it still fails, ask the journal office (contact form) to send a new link.

codes.title: Link expired
codes.meaning: Agreement, reset and invitation links are valid for a limited time (24 hours to 30 days).
codes.fix: Ask the journal office to resend it. Admins: Editorial team → Resend, and choose how many days the new link lasts.

codes.title: Please check the form
codes.meaning: Something required is missing or in the wrong format. The message says exactly what.
codes.fix: Correct the field named in the message and try again.

codes.title: Not possible at this stage
codes.meaning: The manuscript, appointment or campaign is at a stage where this action is not allowed (for example, editing a submitted manuscript or sending a campaign twice).
codes.fix: Refresh the page to see the current stage. Some actions are only available to the editorial office.

codes.title: GitHub token not accepted
codes.meaning: The GitHub token is missing, wrong or expired, so AES cannot update the website.
codes.fix: Admin → Settings → GitHub: paste a new fine-grained token (Contents: read and write, Actions: read-only).

codes.title: Repository or file not found
codes.meaning: The repository name is wrong, the token does not include that repository, or a file AES expected is missing.
codes.fix: Admin → Settings: check the repository is owner/name (e.g. contract-acri/journals) and that the token covers it.

codes.title: GitHub was busy with another change
codes.meaning: Two changes reached GitHub at the same moment.
codes.fix: Wait a few seconds and try again.

codes.title: GitHub error
codes.meaning: GitHub returned an unexpected error.
codes.fix: Try again in a minute. If it repeats, check githubstatus.com and the error log in Admin → Settings.

codes.title: Website build not finished
codes.meaning: The step needs the website to be updated first (for example the proof page or PDF is not live yet).
codes.fix: Wait 3–5 minutes and check GitHub → Actions. A red build means the website could not be updated.

codes.title: Zenodo token not accepted
codes.meaning: The Zenodo token is missing, wrong, from the sandbox instead of zenodo.org (or the other way round), or lacks deposit permissions.
codes.fix: Admin → Settings → Zenodo: paste a token with deposit:write and deposit:actions, and check the Mode setting.

codes.title: Zenodo rejected the details
codes.meaning: One of the article details was refused by Zenodo. The message gives Zenodo's reason.
codes.fix: Correct the article details (Edit article source) and register again.

codes.title: PDF or deposit not found
codes.meaning: AES could not find the article PDF, or the reserved Zenodo deposit no longer exists.
codes.fix: Make sure the website build finished and the PDF opens. If the deposit was deleted on Zenodo, reserve a new DOI.

codes.title: Zenodo error
codes.meaning: Zenodo returned an unexpected error or is under maintenance.
codes.fix: Try again later. Check status on zenodo.org.

codes.title: Email service key not accepted
codes.meaning: The ZeptoMail or Brevo key is missing or wrong.
codes.fix: Admin → Settings → Email sending: paste the correct key, then Send me a test email.

codes.title: Email refused
codes.meaning: The email service refused the message, usually because the sender address or domain is not verified.
codes.fix: Verify the sending domain and sender address in ZeptoMail (workflow) or Brevo (campaigns).

codes.title: Daily email limit reached
codes.meaning: The Gmail fallback or the email service has hit its daily limit.
codes.fix: Connect ZeptoMail, or wait until tomorrow.

codes.title: Server busy
codes.meaning: Google Apps Script is handling too many requests or took too long. AES already retried automatically.
codes.fix: Wait a moment and click Try again.

codes.title: Database sheet missing
codes.meaning: A sheet AES needs does not exist yet, usually after an update.
codes.fix: In Apps Script, run setup() once.

codes.title: File not found in Drive
codes.meaning: A manuscript, letter or signature file was moved, deleted or is not accessible.
codes.fix: Check the ACRI Journals folder in Google Drive, or upload the file again.

codes.title: Unexpected error
codes.meaning: Something went wrong that AES does not recognise.
codes.fix: Note the reference number and send it to the admin. Admins can find it in Admin → Settings → Error log.

codes.title: Cannot reach AES
codes.meaning: Your connection dropped, or the server did not answer after three tries.
codes.fix: Check your internet connection and click Try again.

codes.title: Page did not load completely
codes.meaning: The page finished loading in an unexpected state, often after clicking away very quickly.
codes.fix: AES reloads the page once automatically. If it repeats, click Try again or refresh with Ctrl+Shift+R.

codes.title: Portal not connected
codes.meaning: The portal does not know the address of the AES server.
codes.fix: Set ACRIJ_API in /portal/index.html to the Apps Script web app URL.
